photo.tipsTitle: How to take a good photo

tips.1: Use a plain white sheet of paper (A4 or Letter) lying flat.
tips.2: Put it on a contrasting surface: a dark or coloured table, not a white one, so the sheet is easy to find.
tips.3: Keep the tools apart from each other and from the edge of the paper; nothing should touch.
tips.4: Shoot straight from above, with the camera parallel to the table and the whole sheet in the frame.
tips.5: Shoot from a distance and zoom in rather than coming close: it reduces perspective and the apparent growth of tall tools.
tips.6: Use the flash or bright, even light. Soft shadows are handled, but a flash gives the cleanest outline; avoid strong light from the side.
tips.7: Dark or coloured tools work best; white or chrome parts on white paper may be missed.

site.motivation: Gridfinity is an open standard, and I believe the tools for it should be free too: no accounts, no paywalls, nothing to install. Everything runs in your browser. The other tools here (keychains, rack parts, photo cutouts) are things I make for myself and use myself, and I am simply sharing them.

footer.label: About this site
footer.donate: If PrintKit saved you time, you can say thanks with USDT on the TRON network (TRC20). Donations are optional.

consent.label: Analytics consent
consent.text: We would like to count visits to see how the site is used. This sets a cookie and sends page addresses and general visit data (browser, country) to an analytics service. Your photos, files and settings are never sent. Nothing is loaded until you accept.

size.title: Size
size.toleranceHelp: Makes the panel 0.45 mm lower so neighbouring panels fit. The mounting holes stay on the standard grid.

ears.title: Ears
ears.help: Holes sit 236.525 mm apart. All three: 6.35, 22.225 and 38.1 mm in every unit; outer two: the first and last in every unit; edges only: four holes, the lowest and the highest, whatever the number of units.

pattern.title: Pattern
pattern.help: Only whole elements that fit the window between the ears are cut, centred.
pattern.hicksHelp: Nested hexagon outlines: strokes stay as material, whitespace is cut through. Bridges keep it in one piece.
pattern.asanohaHelp: Asanoha is cut through: the strokes stay as material and the openings between them are cut. Only whole openings are cut. A detail stroke width of 0 leaves plain triangles.

back.title: Back wall
back.help: A separate thin part behind the panel, so the pattern shows another colour. It is exported as a separate object.

device.title: Device
device.help: The shell is the device plus the gap and the wall on every side, open at the back.

shell.title: Shell
shell.raised: Raised to {{u}} U: the device needs it.
shell.help: Printed front plate down, the shell roof bridges over the device width.

front.title: Front plate
front.help: Keystone sockets hold a standard jack behind the plate; a hole can serve any purpose. One per row makes a column, as many as the count a row, in between a grid. Groups in one zone go outward from the shell and stay clear of the ears.
front.zoneNote: Zones above and below need a plate taller than the shell.

vents.title: Vents
vents.enabled: Hexagonal vents on the top and sides
vents.help: Cut through the wall only, away from the edges and the plate.

plate.title: Plate
plate.openHelp: The front is open above the floor between the side walls: only the ears and a strip at the floor remain, as on a sheet-metal shelf.
plate.closedHelp: The plate closes the front. It can be ventilated with a pattern above the floor.

body.title: Shelf
body.help: The front face prints on the bed and the floor and the side walls grow upward from it. A side wall height of 0 removes the walls; they slope in a straight line down to the floor at the back. Pattern "None" gives a solid floor.
